production.note: US model years of the base AMG GT coupe. First: MBUSA's '2017 Mercedes-AMG GT and GT S Specifications' has an AMG GT column (456 hp). MBUSA's 2018 sheet and quick reference guide ('In dealers by summer, 2017') cover the 2018 car (mbusa-2018-gt-specs, mbusa-2018-gt-qrg). Hagerty reports the 2021 base model at 523 hp, 'up from 469 in the 2020 models' (hagerty-2021-amg-gt). Last: Cars.com lists an 'AMG GT Coupe' trim for 2021 (carscom-2021-amg-gt) and describes the generation as '2016-2021 AMG GT', with no 2022 or 2023 model year shown (carscom-2022-amg-gt). See reviewNotes. The AMG GT Roadster (from 2018), GT S, GT C, GT R and Black Series are not part of this record.

body.note: 'Two-door, two passenger coupe'. The base AMG GT Roadster is sold under its own name and is not part of this record.

displacementL.note: 3,982 cc ('Displacement (cc) | 3,982'); marketed as 4.0L. The 2017 sheet gives the same.

fuel.note: Inferred from the sheet's description of the V8 biturbo petrol engine.

transmission.note: 'Transmission Type | AMG 7-Speed DCT Dual-Clutch' (AMG SPEEDSHIFT DCT 7-speed transaxle per mbusa-2018-gt-qrg); the 2017 sheet gives the same.

powerHp.note: Reference model year 2018. Quote: "Horsepower @ rpm | 469 @ 6,000" (GT S column: 515 @ 6,000). Quick reference guide (mbusa-2018-gt-qrg): "4.0L V8 biturbo engine with 469 hp / 465 lb-ft of torque (M178)". US ratings over the run: 456 hp for 2017 (mbusa-2017-gt-specs: "Horsepower @ rpm | 456 @ 6,000"), 469 hp for 2018-2020, and 523 hp for 2021 (hagerty-2021-amg-gt: "523 hp, up from 469 in the 2020 models"). 469 hp covers three of the five model years.

weightLb.note: US curb weight, coupe with the only transmission (7-speed DCT), 2018 model. Quote: "Curb Weight (lbs) | 3,560" (GT S: 3,627). The 2018 quick reference guide and the 2017 sheet give the same 3,560 lb (mbusa-2018-gt-qrg, mbusa-2017-gt-specs).

reviewNotes: (1) The last US model year (2021) rests on Cars.com listings (generation shown as 2016-2021, no 2022 or 2023 page content); no MBUSA page for a 2021 or later base AMG GT was opened. If a 2022 base coupe was sold, 469 hp would cover only three of six years and the reference-year rule would need revisiting. (2) The 2021 base car was rated 523 hp (Hagerty, a publication; no MBUSA sheet opened), a sizable increase over 469 hp; decide whether a year-split record for 2021 is wanted. It could not be sourced here: no 2021 weight was found.
